messages.content: Find me a documentary about global warming.

function.name: retrieve_scientific_paper
function.description: Fetches the details of scientific research paper based on its topic. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

year.description: Year of publishing of the research paper. If not specified, fetches the most recent paper

author.description: Author of the research paper. If not specified, fetches the paper with most citations

message.content:
Here are a handful of highly‑recommended documentaries that tackle global warming (climate change) from different angles—scientific, political, personal, and cinematic.  All of them are available on major streaming platforms or can be rented/purchased online.

| # | Title | Year | Synopsis | Where to Watch |
|---|-------|------|----------|----------------|
| 1 | **An Inconvenient Truth** | 2006 | Former Vice‑President Al Gore’s impassioned presentation of the science of climate change, backed by data and personal anecdotes. | Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, iTunes, Google Play |
| 2 | **An Inconvenient Sequel: Truth to Power** | 2017 | A follow‑up that examines progress (or lack thereof) since 2006, featuring new science, policy updates, and a call to action. | Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, iTunes, Google Play |
| 3 | **Before the Flood** | 2016 | Leonardo DiCaprio travels the world to witness the impacts of climate change, interviewing scientists, activists, and leaders. | Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, iTunes, Google Play |
| 4 | **The 11th Hour** | 2007 | Produced by Leonardo DiCaprio, this film explores the environmental crisis and offers solutions, featuring interviews with scientists, activists, and world leaders. | Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, iTunes, Google Play |
| 5 | **Climate Change: The Facts** | 2019 | A concise, 30‑minute documentary that distills the latest climate science into an easy‑to‑understand format. | YouTube (official channel), Amazon Prime Video |
| 6 | **The Great Global Warming Swindle** | 2007 | A controversial take that questions mainstream climate science; useful for understanding the debate. | Amazon Prime Video, iTunes, Google Play |
| 7 | **The Day After Tomorrow** (fictional) | 2004 | While a Hollywood disaster film, it dramatizes the potential rapid climate shifts and serves as a conversation starter. | Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, iTunes, Google Play |
| 8 | **Our Planet** (Series) | 2019 | Though broader than just warming, each episode highlights how climate change threatens ecosystems worldwide. | Netflix |
| 9 | **The Last Green Planet** (Sci‑Fi) | 2019 | A speculative look at a future where Earth’s climate has drastically changed; good for visualizing long‑term impacts. | Amazon Prime Video, iTunes, Google Play |
|10 | **The Climate Reality Project – Climate Change 101** | 2020 | Short, educational videos that explain the science and policy of climate change. | YouTube (Climate Reality Project channel) |

### How to Choose

| Goal | Recommended Pick |
|------|------------------|
| **Deep dive into science** | *An Inconvenient Truth* / *Climate Change: The Facts* |
| **Policy & activism** | *Before the Flood* / *The 11th Hour* |
| **Visual storytelling** | *Our Planet* (series) |
| **Debate & critical thinking** | *The Great Global Warming Swindle* |
| **Quick overview** | *Climate Change: The Facts* (30 min) |

Feel free to let me know if you’d like more details on any of these, or if you’re looking for something specific (e.g., a documentary focused on a particular region or demographic).
